intro: A model evaluation changes when extra test rows arrive, even though the training data is unchanged. Investigate the supplied scaler: which rows are allowed to determine its statistics?
task: Repair standardize_split. Return a dictionary containing mean, scale, train, and test as NumPy arrays. Fit feature statistics on train only and apply that same transform to both matrices.
requirements: train is a nonempty (n, d) matrix. test is an (m, d) matrix; m may be zero. Require d >= 1.
Use feature-wise population standard deviation (ddof=0). Replace exactly zero standard deviations with one.
Reject incompatible ranks, feature counts, empty training axes, and non-finite values with ValueError. Checks use moderate finite values.
Do not modify either input. A feature constant in train can be nonzero after transforming test; do not force that column to zero.

hints.title: Identify the leak
hints.body: The starter stacks training and test rows before fitting. Predict how adding a test outlier changes its mean.

hints.title: Fit once
hints.body: Compute mean and std along axis=0 of train. Reuse those arrays when transforming test.

hints.title: Handle a constant feature
hints.body: A zero standard deviation would divide by zero. A scale of one preserves the distance from the training constant.

explanation: A preprocessing step learns parameters too. Fitting it on test rows leaks information across the evaluation boundary, even if labels are never used.
The transform subtracts each training feature's mean and divides by its population standard deviation. Broadcasting applies the same learned arrays to every row.
Constant features receive a scale of one. If training always observes five but a test row contains nine, the transformed value is four, not zero.

After repairing the starter, add a distant test row and check that the training transform stays fixed. In a real pipeline, validation and test sets also reuse the training statistics; distribution shift should be observed, not silently normalized away.
